catalog_quote: JFG is a stress language. Each content word or polysyllabic function word has a stressed syllable, indicated (when available) with an acute stress throughout this chapter. The stress generally falls on the lexical root of nouns and verbs: gu.láar [PREF.ROOT] 'slap (n.)'. When the root is longer than one syllable, the stress preferably falls: (i) on the first syllable of the root: a-káañɪñ.ɪ [PREF-ROOT.SUF] 's/he dares', a.lápac [PREF.ROOT] 'gnat', déegen 'yesterday', fébbi 'goat', gu.láamək [PREF.ROOT] 'oar'; (ii) otherwise on the heaviest syllable (e.g. consonantal coda): a.ŋɪmíñ [PREF.ROOT] 'caterpillar', bə.tilimbón [PREF.ROOT] 'flute'. When many suffixes are added to a root, the stress may fall on one of these: gu.saf.undín.ah [PREF.ROOT.SUF.SUF] 'whining (=whine.DVN)'. The stress seems to only have a demarcative function and no lexical minimal pairs based on stress have been found.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Djifanghor Nyun has one stressed syllable per content word (and per polysyllabic function word). Stress goes to the lexical root, not to the class prefix: in a prefix+root word it is the root syllable (gu.láar); in a polysyllabic root it prefers the first root syllable (déegen, fébbi, gu.láamək), otherwise the heaviest syllable, e.g. one with a consonantal coda (a.ŋɪmíñ, bə.tilimbón); when several suffixes follow the root stress may land on a suffix (gu.saf.undín.ah). Long vowels are always stressed and schwa (reduced prefix/suffix vowels) almost never is. Stress is purely demarcative: no minimal pairs. Quint 2022 (p. 181 n. 13) adds that the language is non-tonal.
new_statements.exceptions: Root-initial placement is 'preferred', not absolute: heaviest-syllable placement when the root is polysyllabic and the first syllable is not the heaviest; with multiple suffixes the stress may fall on a suffix (gu.saf.undín.ah 'whining'). Stress marked 'when available', i.e. not established for every lexeme.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: 'each content word or polysyllabic function word has a stressed syllable'; based on ~1,500 lexical items from fieldwork (2011-2014), no acoustic measurements (the chapter says none were made for ATR either). Describes Djifanghor Nyun (Gufangor, village of Djifanghor), not the Djibonker variety (Gubëeher).
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes Djifanghor Nyun (JFG, 'gufuñun' of the village of Djifanghor, ca. 500 speakers) = the Gufangor member of Glottolog gube1234 'Gubeeher-Gufangor-Gubelor', which lumps the three Southwestern Nyun varieties of Djifanghor, Djibonker (Gubëeher) and Djibelor (Gubelor); Quint 2024 p. 291 calls them 'clearly related and probably mutually intelligible' but different 'at all levels of their grammar'. For Gubëeher (Djibonker) proper the accessible description (Cobbinah 2013 thesis, held by the project) is silent on stress, and Cobbinah's 2024 OUP sketch (not accessible) says on its last page that 'the role and nature of stress' still needs research. Quint 2022 (Djifanghor) independently states the language is non-tonal with a marked 'accent tonique'. No Glottolog code exists separately for Gufangor.
